intro: People have played for a very long time. More than 3,000 years ago, people in Mexico made rubber balls. Greeks ran races at Olympia. People in northern Europe made skates from bones.
Each kind of play needs its own place. Soccer needs a pitch. Basketball began in a gym in 1891. Races need a track. Swimmers need a pool. Hockey needs a rink.
Play also needs fair turns. You will meet stone starting lines, a whistle, colored cards and numbers on shirts. You will be able to name a place for each game and tell how people share a turn.
bigQuestion: How do places and shared signals help many people play one game?

timeline.t: Tradition says the first Olympic Games are held at Olympia, Greece
Clubs form the Football Association in London
First organized indoor ice hockey game, in Montreal
The International Football Association Board is formed
James Naismith makes basketball in Springfield, Massachusetts
The soccer referee moves onto the field
First modern Olympic Games open in Athens
London builds a pool inside its Olympic stadium
Women swim in the Olympic Games for the first time
The New York Yankees wear numbers by batting order
Yellow and red cards are first used at the World Cup

words.d: a flat place with edges, built for a game
a place built for races and games, with room for people to watch
a path with lanes, built for running races
a tank of water with a measured length, built for swimming
a sheet of ice with walls around it, built for skating or hockey
the official who is in charge of a game
leaving the starting line before the signal
a sign that sends a message without words

test.q: Which place was built for ice hockey in Montreal in 1875?
test.why: The 1875 game was played inside the Victoria Skating Rink.

test.q: What were the very old balls from Mexico made of?
test.why: People in Mexico made balls from rubber, which comes from tree sap.

test.q: Which group was formed in London in 1863?
test.why: Clubs formed the Football Association in London on 26 October 1863.
James Naismith made basketball in a Springfield gym in 1891.

test.q: What was the balbis at Olympia?
test.why: The balbis was the line of stone slabs where runners started.

test.q: Where did Olympic swimmers race in 1896?
test.why: In 1896, swimmers raced in the sea near Athens.

test.q: Why did Walter Wingfield's game need a lawn?
test.why: Lawn tennis was played on a flat area of cut grass.

test.q: What does a yellow card mean in soccer?
test.why: Yellow is a warning; red means the player must leave.

test.q: What happened to soccer umpires after 1891?
choices: They got whistles for the first time.
They moved to the sidelines as linesmen.
test.why: When the referee moved onto the field, the umpires became linesmen.

test.q: Which is true about Babe Ruth's number in 1929?
choices: It showed his place in the batting order.
It showed how many games he won.
He chose it because he was famous.
test.why: Yankee numbers matched the batting order, and Ruth batted third.

write.prompt: Pick one game from this unit. Name its place and one rule or signal. Use two dates from the unit, such as 1863, 1891 or 1970. Tell how the place or the signal helps everyone take a fair turn.
tips: Name the place: pitch, court, track, pool or rink.
Write one date and who was there, like Naismith in 1891.
Tell what the signal or rule lets everyone see.
Use a word from the word list.
